slides.headline: "Altar" is one of the most misunderstood words in the Bible.
Most of us picture furniture.
body: A table. A rail at the front of a church. Something you kneel at, then leave behind.

slides.headline: A sacred place where the spiritual realm meets people on earth.
Which changes the question entirely.
body: Not "do we have an altar in our house?"
But "where does God meet this household?"
Noah builds one after the flood. Abraham builds one after the promise. Elijah repairs one on Carmel.
slides.kicker: In Scripture, the altar marks where a meeting happens. It is a place you go on purpose.

slides.headline: So it is not a religious performance.
body: It is a household deciding where and when it meets with God.
That is a decision, not a talent.

slides.headline: The barrier to entry is not holiness.
Name the place. Name the time.
body: That is all an altar is at the beginning.

slides.headline: You are not building something holy.
slides.kicker: You are showing up where God already promised to be.
